The BriefA new report found that when Perplexity answers questions about which software to buy, nearly 60 percent of the sites it cites barely get visited, and almost a quarter don't rank in the top million websites on earth. Three connected domains, wifitalents.com, worldmetrics.org and gitnux.org, share the same template and the same DNS setup, and together they wrote about 215,000 machine-generated 'best software' pages built to get quoted by AI, not read by people. If you or your team ask an AI which tool to buy, that answer may be leaning on content written for the AI, not for you, so check what it actually cites before you spend money on its say-so.

Level UpThis week, before you act on an AI's software recommendation, ask it which sources it used, then run each one through a free site authority checker. A site with almost no real backlinks or traffic behind it is a sign the 'review' was written to get quoted by AI, not to help an actual buyer. Ahrefs: free Website Authority Checker
